title: OEE Framework
body: ADW has the equipment — trucks and excavators sit at 90%+ mechanical availability — but production still falls short. If you only watch availability, you'll miss where the real losses are hiding: performance and quality.
keyPoints: Availability isn't the whole story. Run Time ÷ Planned Production Time only tells you the machine showed up — not that it worked hard or worked right.

The performance gap is real and it's ours to close. Truck utilization runs 15–25 points below availability, driven by "no location" and "waiting for excavator" — dispatch and face-readiness problems, not mechanical ones.

Quality losses are invisible until you name them. Wrong-tipping at the ROM pad and crusher bin-level stoppages are quality failures in OEE terms — a truck did the cycle, but the tonnes went nowhere useful.
The Kaizen finding backs this up: people and process, not equipment, are the binding constraint. Availability alone overstates what the fleet is actually delivering.
A combined OEE figure isn't computed here yet — but the raw inputs already exist across the A&U workbook, the running-hours log, and the daily production report.
apply: Watch dispatch sequencing at the loading face — every truck standing idle waiting on an excavator is a performance loss hiding behind a healthy availability number.
